title: What If Gravity Switched Off for 5 Seconds?
lines: For five seconds gravity lets go of the garden, and one small hop puts Gus higher than his roof.
It's ten on a Sunday morning and Gus is flipping a pancake in his garden.
Then gravity switches off. The pancake leaves the pan at eight feet a second and just keeps going.
His neighbor yells that the Earth spins at eight hundred miles an hour, so they'll be flung into space.
His wife sits still. In five seconds the spinning ground sinks ten inches under her chair. That's all.
Don't move, she says. But Gus wants his pancake, so he hops.
That hop is good for one foot. So why is he sailing past his chimney?
You see, gravity is a brake. Roll a ball up a hill and the hill eats its speed.
Take the hill away and the ball rolls on across the floor, as fast as it started.
Gus leaves the lawn at eight feet a second and keeps it all. Four seconds later he's thirty-two feet up.
The pancake left a second sooner at the same speed, so it stays eight feet out of reach.
Then gravity comes back. Gus coasts up one more foot and starts down.
Luckily, that's the height of an Olympic diving tower, and the neighbor has a pool.
Unluckily, Gus is no diver. He hits the water at thirty miles an hour.
A moment later the pancake comes down too, right on Gus.
